predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: Rohilkhand (Katehr): the subahs of Bareilly, Bijnor, Budaun, Moradabad, Pilibhit, Rampur and Shahjahanpur

successors.name: Nawab of Awadh
successors.text: Rohilkhand (Katehr): the subahs of Bareilly, Bijnor, Budaun, Moradabad, Pilibhit, Rampur and Shahjahanpur

ledger.x: 1721: Ali Muhammad Khan makes Rohilkhand independent of the Mughals.
1742: Ali Mohammed Khan annexes parganas of Kumaon.
1772: Mahadji Shinde and the Marathas invade Rohilkhand.
1774: Shuja-ud-Daula, with the East India Company brigade, invades Rohilkhand over the money the Rohillas refused to pay.
23 April 1774: Hafiz Rahmat Khan is killed at Miranpur Katra and Rohilkhand passes to Awadh.
7 October 1774: the Treaty of Lal Dang ends the Rohilla War.

wars.name: Maratha invasion of Rohilkhand
wars.outcome: The Marathas under Mahadji Shinde drove the Rohillas into the hills and took Najibabad for a few weeks; Awadh and the Rohillas signed a treaty on 15 June 1772.

wars.name: Rohilla War
wars.outcome: Awadh and the Company beat the Rohillas at Miranpur Katra on 23 April 1774; Hafiz Rahmat Khan was killed; Rohilkhand fell to Awadh; Faizullah Khan got Rampur by the Treaty of Lal Dang (7 October 1774).

certainty.note: The pages give subahs and towns, not boundaries; the extent in the early decades is not described.
